name: ShadowLynx Forest
summary: Event & attendance platform with mass invoice generation and integrated payment processing. Part of the ShadowLynx ecosystem.
overview: ShadowLynx Forest is a full-cycle event operations platform built for the ShadowLynx ecosystem. It coordinates everything from registration and ticketing through real-time attendance to bulk financial reconciliation — replacing a stack of spreadsheets, mailing lists and manual invoice work with a single product surface.
challenge: Conventions and recurring events generate hundreds of invoices in compressed time windows. The team needed a system that could ingest registrations, verify payments, and emit compliant invoices without a human in the loop, while still allowing operators to override edge cases.
solution: A NestJS service handles the financial pipeline with a queue-based invoice generator, while a NextJS dashboard gives organizers live visibility. PayloadCMS administers content (sessions, speakers, schedules) and the public-facing pages. Payments flow through Stripe with reconciliation jobs that match settlements to invoices nightly.
features: Mass invoice generation with PDF rendering and accounting-system export
Real-time attendance tracking with QR-coded badges
Multi-tenant org structure for the broader ShadowLynx ecosystem
Webhook-driven payment lifecycle with retry & dunning logic
Operator dashboard with audit trail on every financial action

name: Weź Zarezerwuj
summary: Desk reservation system for hybrid open-space offices. Floor plans, recurring bookings and team-aware availability.
overview: A desk reservation product for organizations operating hybrid open-space offices. Built around a visual floor-plan picker rather than a list — booking a desk feels like picking a seat at the cinema.
challenge: Hot-desking only works if employees can find their team and a workable spot in seconds. Most existing tools surface lists of room codes; they ignore the spatial reality of how people choose where to sit.
solution: An interactive SVG floor plan with live availability overlays and team-presence indicators. Recurring booking rules let users lock in their preferred desk for the days they come in, while admins manage zones and capacity.
features: Interactive SVG floor plans with zoom and zone navigation
Team awareness — see where your colleagues are sitting today
Admin tools for zones, capacity and blackout periods

name: RailOps — Corporate Site
summary: Marketing site for an international rail operator. Bilingual content, live timetable embeds, deep CMS-backed editing.
overview: The public face of RailOps — a corporate site that must speak to investors, regulators, prospective B2B customers and the curious public, in two languages, without becoming brittle every time a route changes.
challenge: Rail operators publish constantly: route additions, service notices, press releases, regulatory updates. The site had to give the comms team direct authoring power without involving a developer for every edit.
solution: PayloadCMS drives every block on every page. NextJS renders statically with on-demand revalidation. Live timetable widgets pull from the operations API.
features: Bilingual (PL / EN) with full content parity
Live timetable widget pulled from operations API
Press room with structured release archive

name: RailOps Ouroboros
summary: Operations platform for international and domestic rail. Traction calculations, document generation, project management.
overview: Ouroboros is the operational nervous system for RailOps — the tool dispatchers, route engineers and document specialists actually live in. It plans trains, calculates traction, generates regulatory paperwork, and ties projects to schedules across multiple national networks.
challenge: International rail is a thicket of incompatible standards: signalling, traction power, paperwork, languages, time zones. Operators stitch this together with tribal knowledge and a Frankenstack of vendor tools. The brief: replace it.
solution: A modular NestJS backend with domain services for traction physics, route planning, and document generation. A NextJS operations console that gives dispatchers a single pane for projects, runs and paperwork. Carefully scoped permissions because actions in this system have real-world consequences.
features: Traction physics engine for energy and time calculations
Project & milestone tracking tied to operational runs
Audit-grade change history on every operational entity
Role-based access for dispatchers, planners and auditors

name: RailOps GTFS Live
summary: Live tracking system for public transit vehicles with public-facing map. GTFS-RT ingestion at scale.
overview: A real-time public transit tracking service: it ingests GTFS-Realtime feeds from multiple operators, normalizes them, and serves them to a public map and to downstream systems.
challenge: Live transit feeds arrive in different shapes and at different cadences. Riders want a single map; operators want a single API.
solution: A streaming NestJS pipeline normalizes incoming feeds, deduplicates vehicle reports, and broadcasts diffs over WebSockets to a NextJS map app.
features: GTFS-Realtime ingestion across multiple operator feeds

name: SilFur — Corporate Site
summary: Brand-driven corporate site for a community-focused organization. CMS-backed, fully bilingual.
overview: A polished marketing site for SilFur — the public anchor for the convention system that runs underneath it.
challenge: A community brand needs warmth without sacrificing professionalism, and self-edit power for a small team.
solution: SvelteKit on the front, Payload on the back. The visual system intentionally diverges from the convention app while sharing identity primitives.

name: SilFur Convention System
summary: Conference platform: attendance, hotel-room claiming, scheduling, agenda, integrated payments.
overview: The operational system behind SilFur conventions. Handles registration, hotel room claiming with roommate matching, dynamic scheduling, and the on-site mobile companion.
challenge: Conventions are a frenzy of micro-decisions: who shares a room, who is on which panel, who paid, who showed up. Spreadsheet workflows collapse the moment something changes.
solution: A NestJS API drives a NextJS organizer console and an Expo-based attendee app. Payments through Stripe; rooms with a claim-and-confirm flow that prevents double-booking and surfaces roommate compatibility.
features: Hotel room claiming with roommate matching

name: Fuzzler
summary: Microsite for an annual convention with playful, motion-rich brand expression.
overview: A short-lived but high-impact microsite for an annual convention — playful, motion-rich, and unapologetically branded.
challenge: Stand out in a crowded convention calendar with a one-page experience that earns shares.
solution: A Svelte page built around a single hero animation, with a tightly-scoped scroll choreography.

name: Warszawski Frustuitwalk
summary: Microsite for an annual Warsaw event. Wayfinding, schedule, simple registration.
overview: The web home for an annual event in Warsaw — wayfinding, schedule, registration, all in one focused page.
challenge: Make the event easy to discover, easy to attend, easy to share.
solution: A single tightly-edited NextJS page with map embeds, schedule, and a registration funnel.

name: Ameliówka — Reservations
summary: Internal reservation system for stage and conference room bookings. Client management, internal hotel ops.
overview: An internal reservation system for a hotel — stage and conference room bookings, client management, internal-only operations tooling. No public-facing surface.
challenge: The team had outgrown the spreadsheet-and-phone-call workflow. Bookings clashed, double-quotes leaked out, history was lost.
solution: A purpose-built internal app: clients, contacts, room calendar, quotes, contracts. Hono API, NextJS admin console.
